study type: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
cohort: The study included 208 infants born to mothers with pre-pregnancy BMI between 28 and 45 kg/m2 who completed the APPROACH study.
finding: Limiting gestational weight gain (GWG) among women with pre-pregnancy overweight or obesity was associated with lower infant weight, BMI z-score, weight z-score, and abdominal circumference at birth.
mod_finding: Gestational weight gain below the Institute of Medicine guideline of a maximum of 9 kg was associated with fewer emergency cesarean deliveries.
birth_weight: Infants in the lowest GWG quartile had an average birth weight of 3,420 g, and overall, limiting GWG was associated with lower birthweight.
